jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position in Preclinical Development of Bicyclic Peptides for Nuclear Medicine (Biochemiker/in)
jobs.description: The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.The DKFZ is a place where the brightest minds pursue bold ideas and seek answers to pioneering scientific questions through collaboration, innovation, and exploration across many disciplines. We provide a dynamic environment which empowers excellence with state-of-the-art technologies, cutting edge infrastructure, and a global scientific network. Contribute your knowledge, vision, and dedication to create a space where scientific discovery in cancer research is transformed into benefits for human health.Together with selected university partner sites, the DKFZ has established the German Cancer Consortium (DKTK) (https://dktk.dkfz.de/en) . The alliance between the DKFZ as the core center and the university partner sites in Berlin, Dresden, Essen/Düsseldorf, Frankfurt/Mainz, Freiburg, Heidelberg, Munich, and Tübingen operates joint translation centers at the University Medical Centers of each of the selected partner sites. The DKTK contributes significantly to filling the translational gap between basic and clinical cancer research, thereby developing new strategies for personalized oncology in prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cancer. DKTK conducts transformative translational cancer research, educates the next generation of translation-oriented medical and clinical scientists and establishes strong pipelines towards clinical cancer research and the economy.At the DKTK partner site Freiburg, we are offering, starting at the earliest date possible, a Postdoc Position in Preclinical Development of Bicyclic Peptides for Nuclear Medicine.The Division of Radiopharmaceutical Development at DKTK Freiburg focuses on the development and clinical translation of novel radiopharmaceuticals for molecular imaging and targeted radionuclide therapy. A key emphasis is on radiotheranostics, from the identification of new targets and tumor-targeting compounds to preclinical evaluation and first-in-human translation.The position is located at the University Medical Center Freiburg, Department of Nuclear Medicine (www.uniklinik-freiburg.de/nuklearmedizin/radiopharmakaentwicklung).Your TasksThe position is part of a long-term collaboration with the company Bicycle Therapeutics (https://www.bicycletherapeutics.com/)  and covers the preclinical characterization of novel bicyclic peptides for clinical translation. This established and successful research platform includes the identification and evaluation of novel radiopharmaceuticals for positron emission tomography (PET) and radionuclide therapy. The relationship between DKFZ and Bicycle Therapeutics has expanded to include a more continuous and purpose-driven commitment towards advancing candidates towards the clinic. The current project aims at the preclinical development and clinical translation of novel radiolabeled, tumor-targeting bicyclic peptide conjugates for diagnostic and therapeutic application in nuclear medicine. The bicyclic peptide conjugates are synthesized by solid phase synthesis and modified by bioconjugation chemistry. Finally, the conjugates are labeled with several clinically relevant radioisotopes for in vitro and in vivo evaluation. Your task is to elaborate the scientific data within this work plan and to communicate the results with our collaboration partner. Your Profile- Master's degree and PhD in biochemistry, chemistry or pharmacy or equivalent- Experience in peptide chemistry and related analytical methods- Experience in biological assays and in vivo experiments would be advantageous- Good communication skills in English- Motivation to work in an interdisciplinary team- Interest in application-oriented / translational researchTo apply, please submit a brief cover letter stating your motivation, a curriculum vitae as well as certified copies of your university degrees with grades (BA and MA certificate / Diploma / PhD certificate) and contact details of two referees via our online application portal.We Offer- Excellent framework conditions: state-of-the-art equipment and opportunities for international networking at the highest level- Remuneration according to TV-L incl. occupational pension plan and capital-forming payments- 30 days of vacation per year- Flexible working hours- Possibility of mobile work and part-time work- Family-friendly working environment- Sustainable travel to work: subsidized Germany job ticket- Our Corporate Health Management Program offers a holistic approach to your well-being- Develop your full potential: access to the DKFZ International Postdoc Program and DKFZ Career Service with targeted offers for your personal development to further develop your talentsAre you interested?Then become part of the DKFZ and join us in contributing to a life without cancer!Contact:Prof. Dr. Matthias EderPhone: +49 761270 74220Duration: The position is initially limited to 2 years with the possibility of prolongation.Application Deadline: November 05, 2026Applications by e-mail cannot be accepted.Please also note that we cannot return applications submitted by post.We are convinced that an innovative research and working environment thrives on the diversity of its employees. Therefore, we welcome applications from talented people, regardless of gender, cultural background, nationality, ethnicity, sexual identity, physical ability, religion and age. People with severe disabilities are given preference if they have the same aptitude.Notice: We are subject to the regulations of the Infection Protection Act (IfSG). Therefore, all our employees must provide proof of immunity against measles.

jobs.employer_name: Siemens Energy Global GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day As a Government Affairs Manager at Siemens Energy, you will help shape the political, regulatory, and geopolitical environment in which we operate. You will translate policy developments into business opportunities, build trusted relationships with government stakeholders, and support Siemens Energy’s leadership in advancing the global energy transition.Working closely with Business Areas, regional leadership (Hubs), and Executive Board Members, you will identify emerging political trends, assess risks and opportunities, and develop advocacy strategies that support the company’s growth agenda. You will be the interlink to and representative for selected HUBs and the corporate Government Affairs department. Your work will directly contribute to creating favorable market conditions for energy infrastructure, decarbonization technologies, grid modernization, and energy security solutions. How You’ll Make an Impact * Monitoring and analysis of political, regulatory, and geopolitical developments* Advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and relationship management across key public and industry stakeholders* Political positioning and policy support aligned with Siemens Energy’s strategic priorities* Identification of policy-driven business opportunities, including incentives, industrial policy, and funding programs* Preparation of executive briefings, talking points, stakeholder dossiers, and strategic assessments* Cross-functional coordination and external representation to strengthen Siemens Energy’s positioning in the global energy transitionWhat You Bring* Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, International Relations, Economics, Law, or a related field* Several years of professional experience in Government Affairs, Public Affairs, Public Policy, Regulatory Affairs, diplomacy, consulting, or related fields* Strong understanding of European and international energy policy, industrial policy, and geopolitical developments* Proven stakeholder management, analytical, strategic, and communication skills, including executive-level presentations and briefing materials* Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced international environment, manage multiple priorities, and demonstrate high integrity and commitment to compliance* Fluent English and good German; additional languages advantageousAbout the TeamThe Government Affairs department supports Siemens Energy's mission to become the world's most valued energy technology company. We connect business priorities with public policy, identify geopolitical risks and opportunities, and work with governments and institutions to promote energy security, industrial competitiveness, and decarbonization. jobs.description: The German Cancer Research Center (DKFZ) is one of Europe’s largest cancer research centers. “Research for a life without cancer" is the mission of our world-class scientists and all our team members.We investigate how cancer develops, identify cancer risk factors and search for new cancer prevention strategies. We develop new methods with which tumors can be diagnosed more precisely and cancer patients can be treated more successfully. Every contribution counts – whether in research, administration or infrastructure. This is what makes our daily work so meaningful and exciting.The Single-cell Open Lab at the German Cancer Research Center is seeking, starting in January 2027, a Staff Scientist as Parental Leave Replacement.The Single-cell Open Lab (scOpenLab) provides state-of-the-art infrastructure and scientific expertise for single-cell sequencing and spatial omics. Our goal is to enable researchers to perform advanced experiments independently: we advise users on experimental design, provide hands-on training, and support them throughout project optimization, experimental implementation, and library preparation.Our technology portfolio covers a broad range of single-cell and multi-omic approaches, including single-cell RNA, DNA, and chromatin profiling, as well as spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics. Beyond providing access to established technologies, method development is an important part of our work. We continuously evaluate, adapt, and establish emerging single-cell and spatial technologies and develop customized experimental workflows. Examples include HIPSDR-seq for joint single-cell DNA and RNA profiling and the implementation of new spatial omics approaches. The scOpenLab is also closely involved in MultiSpace, the platform for spatial omics within the Health + Life Science Alliance Heidelberg Mannheim. Through MultiSpace, we collaborate with other technology platforms and research groups to enable multimodal spatial profiling and the integration of spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, and other molecular readouts.Your TasksWe are looking for a research scientist to cover a period of parental leave and join our interdisciplinary team. The position combines user support and training with hands-on experimental work and technology development, offering the opportunity to work at the forefront of rapidly evolving single-cell and spatial omics technologies with the following tasks:- Planning and designing spatially resolved transcriptome and proteomics projects with our users- Training of new users for spatial and single-cell omics assays- Optimization and integration of new methods in the lab with a focus on multimodal approaches- Organizing and driving early access programmes- Scheduling and maintenance of service infrastructure for image-based spatial transcriptomicsYour Profile- University degree in life science (MSc), additional PhD preferred- Experience and very good knowledge of NGS techniques, library preparation, tissue handling, and imaging (skills in data analysis are a plus)- Previous work in the single-cell field is certainly an advantage- Very good knowledge of English and German- Self-motivation and innovative thinking will be required for the successful implementation of your work.
